9ad9a77ab1cb: In a family where children were named after their grandparents in every generation — and where a new wife could give her daughter the name of the dead first wife — the same four or five names come round again and again. Here the namesakes are set side by side, so they can be told apart.
b8b848965e30: A rule of thumb: <t1>-sen</t1> and <t2>-datter</t2> tell you who the father was — Jansdatter is Jan’s daughter, Ibsdatter is Ib’s daughter. <t3>Klit</t3> and <t4>Silkjær</t4>, on the other hand, tell you where people lived. The first dies with the generation; the second can be inherited.
e8b164d12d8e: <t1>1855—1928</t1><t2><t3>Niels Thomsen Silkjær</t3> — the one who made Silkjær a fixed, heritable family name. Smallholder, fisherman and boatman in Økjær.</t2>
a6638db402df: <t1>1910—1986</t1><t2><t3>Niels Silkær</t3> — the fishing skipper’s son, born at Årgab. Ran arms across the North Sea in 1945 and owned E.94 until 1976.</t2>
9e4474bde4ca: <t1>1909—1972</t1><t2><t3>Niels Silkjær Madsen</t3> — Ane Johanne’s son. Bore his mother’s family name as a middle name; married in Isenvad in 1933 and died in Ikast in 1972.</t2>
d7a35b8e480c: <t1>1911—1986</t1><t2><t3>Niels Silkjær Lauridsen</t3> — Ane Marie’s son. Smallholder at Damhus, Sønder Nissum. The boy in the school photograph of 1919.</t2>
1e6d726ac414: <t1>1914—</t1><t2><t3>Niels Silkjær</t3> — Jens Klaus’ son at Oustrup on Djursland, born on 28 February. Here Silkjær is purely a surname.</t2>
d46a6ece0261: <t1>1914—1999</t1><t2><t3>Niels Silkjær</t3> — Esper’s son in Gudum, born the same year as his cousin on Djursland, on 17 November — exactly the same name, two sides of Jutland. A farmer in Gudum with eight children; died in Struer.</t2>
9f02dbfd39da: <t1>1915—1996</t1><t2><t3>Niels Silkjær Bøndergaard</t3> — Karen Marie’s son. Fisherman and tanker-boat master in Esbjerg.</t2>
6ed2885ea938: <t1> </t1><t2><t3>Niels Kristian Silkjær Burkarl</t3> — Ellen Nielsen Silkjær’s son; one of seven named children in the Burkarl branch, where all seven carried Silkjær on as part of their names.</t2>
c9eefef8be97: a wife, a daughter, a grandchild
a84d8aeab945: <t1>1843—1880</t1><t2><t3>Ane Johanne Kristensen</t3> — Niels Thomsen’s <t4>first</t4> wife, twelve years older than he. Died in Økjær half a year after her only childbirth.</t2>
52b62ba82619: <t1>1883—1956</t1><t2><t3>Ane Johanne Nielsen Silkjær</t3> — his daughter by his second wife, named after the first. Married to the master mason Mads Erik Madsen; the pivot of the chronicle, chapter 14.</t2>
7bfa836e3455: <t1>1909—</t1><t2><t3>Ane Johanne Lauridsen</t3> — the granddaughter, named after her aunt. Daughter of Ane Marie in Husby.</t2>
0547e840e0f7: Anne Marie, Ane Marie / Ane Kirstine
fe9d8f8050c1: and a cutter with almost the same name
45766c64759f: <t1>1827—1863</t1><t2><t3>Anne Marie Jansdatter Tarpgaard</t3> — a farmer’s daughter from Vedersø, married to Thomas Jensen. Died in Økjær at 35.</t2>
8963a06121d1: <t1>b. 1837</t1><t2><t3>Anne Marie Jensdatter</t3> — Thomas Jensen’s sister from Husby Klit, married to Anders Knudsen Øe — in all likelihood the beach bailiff who drowned together with her brother in 1878, while her brother Esper survived. It is she who makes the boat one of two brothers and a brother-in-law (chapter 5).</t2>
f08b98c8da28: <t1>1880—1960</t1><t2><t3>Ane Marie Nielsen Silkjær</t3> — her son’s daughter and namesake. The eldest of the brothers and sisters, married name Lauridsen, stayed in Husby all her life.</t2>
b53237cc016a: <t1>1892—1977</t1><t2><t3>Ane Kirstine Nielsen Silkjær</t3> — the sister, married on New Year’s Day 1920 in Nysogn Church to the fisherman Christen Tarbensen; their four children had Silkjær in their names. Not to be confused with <t4>Ane Kirstine Silkjær, née Hansen</t4> (1910—1969), the wife of her nephew Niels.</t2>
45c96d7c49c4: <t1>1897—1990</t1><t2><t3>ANNE KIRSTINE, E.94</t3> — the cutter, in two hulls: the 1897 build and the new Hobro build of 1949, which took over name and number. A vessel, not a person; she is the one chapters 17 and 18 are about.</t2>
890c6bb9a306: three generations, the same first name
9e80baa47c65: <t1>1754—1824</t1><t2><t3>Thomas Nielsen Langager</t3> — smallholder and enrolled seaman in Stadil. Maternal grandfather of the next.</t2>
cb322c72b2ba: <t1>1825—1878</t1><t2><t3>Thomas Jensen</t3> — smallholder and fisherman in Økjær. Lost at sea on 9 November 1878. The first of the family to be recorded with the name Silkjær — in the deed of 1876.</t2>
a202558488fe: <t1>1882—1950</t1><t2><t3>Thomas Nielsen Silkjær</t3> — his grandson. Fishing skipper in Esbjerg, in the registers “T. N. Silkjær”.</t2>
8202d6c6db91: <t1>1917—1997</t1><t2><t3>Laura</t3>, née Madsen — Ane Johanne’s daughter, domestic help, number ten of fourteen.</t2>
4cf395f61b01: <t1>1911—1996</t1><t2><t3>Laurids Mikkelsen</t3> — her husband, owner of Nygaard in Fjelstervang. The names look alike; they are not related.</t2>
56a18bca4464: <t1>c. 1830</t1><t2><t3>Jens Claus</t3> — Ane Jensen’s father, known from the parish book’s list of maternal grandparents.</t2>
a286dc7d53fc: <t1>1886—1959</t1><t2><t3>Jens Klaus Nielsen Silkjær</t3> — his daughter’s son, named after him. Gravedigger at Vejlby Church; founder of the Djursland branch.</t2>
53c3cad3c2fb: <t1>1710—1861</t1><t2><t3>Klit</t3> — the family’s byname while it lived at Sønder Klit and Husby Klit.</t2>
323fd40d45e9: <t1>1876—1905</t1><t2><t3>Silkjær</t3> — the farm name that became the family name in three steps: written on Thomas Jensen in the deed of 1876, used for the children in the census of 1890 and as a byname for Niels Thomsen in the parish register of 1896, and made the lawful family name by Niels’ name certificate of 21 November 1905. The form the family itself writes.</t2>
6a2b39eb869e: <t1>The 1900s</t1><t2><t3>Silkær</t3> — a spelling found in parts of the Esbjerg branch’s parish registers and vessel registers. The same name, just without the j.</t2>
